newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel spurns Arafat offer to fight "terror" -PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel spurns Arafat offer to fight "terror" -PLO.

text.p: Chief PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said on Sunday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had rejected an offer from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to join together "in fighting terror".
Erekat made the comment to CNN television network during an interview covering an attack by two suicide bombers on a Jewish market in Jerusalem that killed 13 people last Wednesday.

"Mr Netanyahu, instead of accepting President Arafat's offer to join him in fighting terror and the enemies of peace, he declared a series of collective punishment measures against the Palestinian people," Erekat said.
"We urge Mr Netanyahu to stop shooting himself in the foot and to accept President Arafat's offer to join together in order to fight the enemies of peace.
"Terror should not be rewarded and so far Mr Netanyahu has suspended the negotiations and that's what the terrorists wanted."

Israeli Ambassador-designate to the United Nations Dore Gold, appearing beside Erekat in the studio, asked directly if Netanyahu had spurned an offer from Arafat, said: "Well, I don't think that's exactly correct".

Gold did not elaborate but said that prior to the attack on Wednesday, Palestinian security officials were conditioning cooperation in the fight against militants on Israel making "certain tangible concessions".
Palestinians have demanded Israel halt Jewish settlement of occupied Arab lands which they say pre-empts peace talks.
Netanyahu's cabinet demanded Arafat crack down on Moslem militants after Wednesday's bombing.

Israel also suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, rounded up scores of suspected militants, closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, demanded the extradition of the PLO police chief and threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job.

A leaflet issued in the name of the militant Islamic Hamas movement claimed responsibility for the twin suicide bombings at the market but Israeli and Palestinian officials say they are not sure of its authenticity.
